basics.name: Nutan Prabhat
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer — Backend & Full-Stack
basics.summary: Senior software engineer with 4+ years building production systems in Python, Django, and DRF, currently sole engineer on an enterprise client account and owning delivery from concept to production. Recent work includes a two-stage visual retrieval system (CLIP embeddings in Qdrant with a feature-based reranker) lifted from a 41.9% baseline to 97.7% Top-1 accuracy, and a multi-tenant Django/DRF and React SaaS platform. Deep SQL background across query optimisation, stored-procedure rewrites, and data-integrity work on live enterprise systems, alongside REST API design, GCP deployment, and CI/CD.

work.name: Aziro Technologies
work.summary: Sole engineer on an enterprise client account, owning the full delivery lifecycle.
highlights: Sole engineer on the account — scoping, HLD/LLD design, development, testing, documentation, and delivery.
Rebuilt a two-stage visual retrieval engine: CLIP ViT-B/16 embeddings in Qdrant for candidate recall, then a feature-based reranker for precision — Top-1 accuracy from a 41.9% baseline to 97.7%.
Built the held-out evaluation harness behind that result, identifying recall as the true ceiling and redirecting the next phase of work.

Delivered a Python desktop CAD validation platform end to end — DXF parsing, 2D computational geometry, spatial indexing, PySide6 UI — with one-click batch processing across drawing folders and a second system integrated in.
Built a JSON-configured rule engine binding validation rules to check and fix functions at runtime, with priority-ordered execution and full audit trails — automating 3+ manual workflows.
Architected both platforms as configuration-driven: new categories, rules, thresholds, and weights are added through JSON without code changes.
Produced full system documentation and test coverage for clean client handover.

work.name: UnKl Games
work.summary: Co-founded a small studio and shipped a live multiplayer title.
highlights: Built and published Pen Fight 2D, a turn-based multiplayer mobile game in Unity (C#), reaching 10K+ downloads on Google Play.
Integrated Google Cloud Platform (Authentication, APIs, Analytics) and Unity Cloud Save, building account and progression sync from scratch.
Built a server-authoritative economy in Node.js with escrow-held fees, idempotent payouts keyed by match ID, dual-client verification, and refund handling.
Architected real-time multiplayer on Unity Relay and Transport, using separate reliable and unreliable channels and choosing raw transport over the netcode framework.
Implemented race-safe match negotiation with single start authority, plus turn timers, disconnect forfeits, and version gating before escrow.
Diagnosed and fixed a cross-device desync from resolution-dependent UI scaling by re-basing the wire protocol on normalised coordinates.
Ran the full release cycle: internal testing tracks, feedback-driven fixes, production rollout, and post-release updates.

work.name: Zenoti
work.summary: Backend and full-stack work on a large multi-tenant enterprise product.
highlights: Primary code reviewer within a year of joining; requested changes on 25+ of 50+ PRs, including work already approved by senior staff. Mentored teammates on defect resolution.
Delivered 5 client-specific and 2 core-team features end to end; 2 were adopted into the core product.
Designed a localization abstraction layer: providers switchable through configuration, per-element opt-out control, and coverage extended through API and database layers.
Diagnosed and optimised SQL queries that had degraded 2–3x, restoring near-baseline response times with no downtime.
Rewrote legacy stored procedures, including one of 4,000 lines, replacing a destructive save pattern with differential updates to eliminate a data-loss risk.
Migrated a large ASP.NET codebase to jQuery 3.5+, taking the highest-complexity pages and contributing refactor patterns adopted into shared libraries.
Extended Elasticsearch type-ahead search with minimum-character filtering and query tuning.

projects.name: CreatorHub
projects.description: Multi-tenant SaaS platform for creator agencies — tenancy, identity, campaign lifecycle and payouts. Built through spec-driven AI development: I architected the module structure and data models, defined the features and UI, directed the implementation in Claude Code, and tested it end to end.
highlights: Architected a 12-app module structure separating tenancy, identity, campaigns and billing concerns.
Designed dual-actor JWT authentication and role-based access control with per-user grant and deny overrides.
Designed an 11-stage forward-only campaign lifecycle with audit trail and milestone-based approvals.

projects.name: Portfolio — JSON-driven site, CV generator and live editor
projects.description: This site, and the pipeline behind it. Two JSON files are the only source of truth: the build derives the website, the downloadable CV PDF, the Open Graph image, sitemap, robots.txt, CNAME and the HTML head from them, so no name, URL or filename is written into code or config. The interesting part is not the page — it is that CI refuses to publish content that does not hold together.
highlights: Content is schema-validated in CI with cross-file rules on top: every skill key must resolve in the asset registry, a section listed with no data fails, CDN icons must be version-pinned, and the phone number may never reach committed JSON. Failures name the offending key. The same validator runs in the pre-commit hook and inside the editor, so all three agree by construction.

One dataset, two artifacts: the site and a Calibri-metric CV PDF are rendered from the same JSON — the PDF printed by Puppeteer against a hidden print route using self-hosted Carlito — so the page and the document I email cannot drift apart.
Performance and accessibility are enforced, not aspired to: Lighthouse thresholds and a 250 KB gzipped JS ceiling both fail the deploy, with reports uploaded as artifacts when they do.

An in-browser editor with sectional saves, live validation and a field-level old-vs-new diff before writing. It writes the JSON directly when run locally, and on the deployed site detects the absent write endpoint and becomes a working read-only demo that exports instead.
Built with Claude Code against a written spec — the validation, budgets and single-source-of-truth constraints are what keep AI-assisted output honest.
